newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Forty-two Indonesians to stand trial for riot.
newsitem.headline: Forty-two Indonesians to stand trial for riot.

text.p: Forty-two Indonesians will face trial soon for their alleged involvement in last month's riot in Tasikmalaya, West Java, in which four people were killed, the official Antara news agency reported on Monday.

West Java police spokesman, Lieutenant Colonel Istanto, was quoted as saying on Sunday the suspects would be tried on charges of arson and that police would soon submit the dossiers to the local prosecutor's office.

Four people died after an angry mob went on a rampage through Tasikmalaya in late December, setting fire to shops, buildings and churches. The violence was apparently sparked by a report of police brutality towards some Moslem religious teachers.

News reports said every police station in the district suffered damage, with three police buildings destroyed by fire. The cost of the damage had been estimated by authorites at 85 billion rupiah ($36 million).
Istanto said the 42 suspects were among the 51 people arrested for their alleged involvement in the riot. Antara said police initially arrested 123 people. The agency gave no further details.
Four policeman were dishonourably discharged last Friday for beating up a Moslem teacher and two of his students, an incident which apparently sparked the Tasikmalaya riot.
Antara reported on Saturday the teacher and two students were brought to the police station on December 23 after they disciplined a pupil who was the son of a local police officer.
The Kompas newspaper said the pupil was disciplined after he was allegedly caught stealing from supermarkets and an Islamic boarding school.
